subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should repair work be authorized from the released-version report, or should the issue first require a current-main capture showing the synthetic value in the final Telegram text or caption payload?
rationale: Current source assigns the strings to different representation owners, so choosing a repair boundary without observing the Telegram handoff risks changing valid model or transcript behavior.

options.title: Capture current-main boundary
options.body: Record the reply payload and Telegram send operation for a failing directive or media-only turn before assigning a source repair.

options.title: Authorize narrow instrumentation
options.body: Allow a bounded diagnostic change that logs redacted representation transitions so a maintainer can identify where visible text is replaced.

options.title: Accept released evidence
options.body: Treat the reported 2026.6.11 behavior as sufficient and sponsor a repair, requiring the implementation to preserve prompt and transcript placeholder contracts.

recommendation.title: Capture current-main boundary
recommendation.body: Record the reply payload and Telegram send operation for a failing directive or media-only turn before assigning a source repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to both the gateway media path and Telegram dispatch lifecycle, making them the strongest available boundary owner.
